thread.title: Peer Review for Project Drafts
thread.content: Review assignments are out for the project drafts and will be due by midnight next Tuesday 11/21. You can access them via the Reviewer console on Microsoft CMT (will look something like the below image): Everyone will have either 1 or 2 reports to review. The questions you need to answer in the review are tailored for this class, so it won't be the same questions as for a typical conference submission. Every paper will have between 2-4 reviews, with a majority having at least 3.If you encounter any problems with submitting reviewers, feel free to ask questions on this thread.UPDATE: To keep workload fair among students, we have updated assignments so that every student will do exactly 1 review (for those who initially had 2, I removed one of yours at random).
thread.document:
Review assignments are out for the project drafts and will be due by midnight next Tuesday 11/21. You can access them via the Reviewer console on Microsoft CMT (will look something like the below image): 

Everyone will have either 1 or 2 reports to review. The questions you need to answer in the review are tailored for this class, so it won't be the same questions as for a typical conference submission. Every paper will have between 2-4 reviews, with a majority having at least 3.

If you encounter any problems with submitting reviewers, feel free to ask questions on this thread.

UPDATE: To keep workload fair among students, we have updated assignments so that every student will do exactly 1 review (for those who initially had 2, I removed one of yours at random).

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Remember your goals while reviewing: </paragraph><paragraph>1) Give the project group feedback that can help them fix bugs, make things more clear, and not have holes in their project. </paragraph><paragraph>2) Exercise your own capabilities for critical evaluation. Your job is not to be nice or generous --- it is to help find and identify things that are unclear, represent logical leaps, find gaps, etc... It is often easier to sharpen these skills looking at somebody else's work because the human side of being in a team or not wanting to feel bad sometimes makes us hold back. But in reality and for your own future, you are going to need the skill of being super critical for your own work. </paragraph><paragraph/><paragraph/></document>
comments.document:
Remember your goals while reviewing: 

1) Give the project group feedback that can help them fix bugs, make things more clear, and not have holes in their project. 

2) Exercise your own capabilities for critical evaluation. Your job is not to be nice or generous --- it is to help find and identify things that are unclear, represent logical leaps, find gaps, etc... It is often easier to sharpen these skills looking at somebody else's work because the human side of being in a team or not wanting to feel bad sometimes makes us hold back. But in reality and for your own future, you are going to need the skill of being super critical for your own work.
